prov.text: For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the PCL, off-balance sheet credit exposures was primarily attributable to an increase in unfunded commitment balances and an increase in the quantitative reserve rates due to changes in the macroeconomic forecast. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the PCL, off-balance sheet credit exposures was primarily attributable to an increase in the quantitative reserve rates due to changes in the macroeconomic forecast and an increase in the utilization rates for unfunded commitments, partially offset by a decrease in commercial construction unfunded commitment balances and positive credit migration. Please see the section captioned “Provision for Credit Losses” for additional information regarding the PCL on LHFI and off-balance sheet credit exposures.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, Trustmark’s combined effective tax rate was 17.6% and 17.8%, respectively, compared to 18.6% and 18.5%, respectively, for the same time periods in 2025. Trustmark’s effective tax rate continues to be less than the statutory rate primarily due to various tax-exempt income items and its utilization of income tax credit programs. Trustmark invests in partnerships that provide income tax credits on a Federal and/or State basis ( i.e. , new market tax credits, low-income housing tax credits or historical tax credits). The income tax credits related to these partnerships are utilized as specifically allowed by income tax law and are recorded as a reduction in income tax expense.

net.text: Trustmark reported net income of $58.1 million, or basic and diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $1.00, in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $56.8 million, or basic and diluted EPS of $0.94, in the third quarter of 2025. Trustmark’s reported performance during the quarter ended September 30, 2026 produced a return on average tangible equity of 12.72%, a return on average assets of 1.21%, an average equity to average assets ratio of 11.24% and a dividend payout ratio of 25.00%, compared to a return on average tangible equity of 12.84%, a return on average assets of 1.21%, an average equity to average assets ratio of 11.26% and a dividend payout ratio of 25.53% during the quarter ended September 30, 2025.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text: Net interest income is the principal component of Trustmark’s income stream and represents the difference, or spread, between interest and fee income generated from earning assets and the interest expense paid on deposits and borrowed funds. Fluctuations in interest rates, as well as volume and mix changes in earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, can materially impact net interest income. The net interest margin is computed by dividing annualized fully taxable equivalent (FTE) net interest income by average interest-earning assets and measures how effectively Trustmark utilizes its interest-earning assets in relationship to the interest cost of funding them. The accompanying yield/rate analysis tables show the average balances for all assets and liabilities of Trustmark and the interest income or expense associated with earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities. The yields and rates have been computed based upon interest income and expense adjusted to an FTE basis using the federal statutory corporate tax rate in effect for each of the periods shown. Loans on nonaccrual have been included in the average loan balances, and interest collected prior to these loans having been placed on nonaccrual has been included in interest income.

intro.text: Trustmark Corporation (Trustmark), a Mississippi business corporation incorporated in 1968, is a bank holding company headquartered in Jackson, Mississippi. As previously disclosed, on August 4, 2025, Trustmark’s principal subsidiary, Trustmark National Bank, initially chartered by the State of Mississippi in 1889, converted from a national banking association to a Mississippi-chartered banking corporation and changed its name to Trustmark Bank (TB). TB is a member bank of the Federal Reserve System and is supervised by the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta (FRBA) and the Mississippi Department of Banking and Consumer Finance (MDBCF). At December 31, 2025, TB had total assets of $18.923 billion, which represented approximately 99.99% of the consolidated assets of Trustmark.
